text:
maria: CI started failing in eu-west-1 on our gitops render step — sops decryption errors seen across 3 pipelines around 09:12 UTC
ashwin: yup seeing it in buildkite logs. minimal error: `sops: failed to decrypt secrets/cluster.yaml: InvalidCiphertextException: CMK not accessible to principal`
deploy-bot: pipeline `gitops/main` failed — step `render-secrets` exit=1
jules: that looks like KMS key policy changed or the key was rotated and the CI principal wasn't put back in the policy
samir: any active key rotations last night? we rotated an audit key but that was separate alias...
maria: i rotated a cross-account audit key but didn't touch `redwood/sops/eu-west-1` alias intentionally. checking console now
ashwin: mitigation options off the top of my head:
- re-add CI role to key policy (fast)
- re-encrypt repo secrets to new key (requires re-issue)
- temporarily switch CI to decrypt via a short-lived deployer key (messy)
jules: prefer re-add role to policy and re-run. don't change encrypted files mid-deploy
maria: confirmed: during rotation automation the new key was created with a restrictive policy (admins only). CI role was dropped. i'm adding the pipeline role back to the key policy now
samir: nice catch. we should also add a smoke test so CI fails earlier (decrypt tiny file) and an alert on KMS decrypt errors
ashwin: agreed — i'll open a 1-line PR to add `sops decrypt` smoke step in the render stage and a Grafana alert for `sops_decrypt_failures > 0`
maria: manual rerun triggered — buildkite #4623
deploy-bot: manual run started by maria — buildkite #4623
maria: build succeeded \ud83c\udf89 secrets rendered and env vars injected across branches
jules: follow-ups:
- add decrypt smoke test in pipeline (ashwin)
- alert on repeated decrypt failures (ashwin)
- add key-rotation runbook checklist to include adding CI principals back to KMS policy (samir)
- consider an alternative flow: sealed-secrets for cluster-only secrets to reduce CI KMS dependency (item for product)
samir: i'll draft the runbook. include commands to inspect/modify key policy: 
```
aws kms get-key-policy --key-id <arn> --policy-name default
aws kms put-key-policy --key-id <arn> --policy-name default --policy file://policy.json
```
maria: thanks. also adding a short note to rotation automation to preserve an allow-list for pipeline roles
ashwin: opening PRs for smoke test + alert rule now, linking to follow-ups board
jules: please add a postmortem note in the incident channel once follow-ups exist
maria: will do. thanks team :thumbsup:
